briefing.headline: OpenAI o4 and DeepSeek-R2 escalate frontier race as compute shortages intensify

sections.label: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
sections.text: The AI race has accelerated with multiple frontier releases in the past week. US export controls on advanced chips continue to shape global deployment patterns while safety concerns mount around agentic systems.

sections.label: FRONTIER MODELS
sections.text: OpenAI released o4 with advanced reasoning capabilities. Anthropic's Claude 4 Opus achieved new multimodal benchmarks. DeepSeek-R2 and xAI's Grok-3 push open-weight performance closer to closed models.

sections.label: SAFETY & SECURITY
sections.text: Prompt injection remains the #1 vulnerability in production AI systems and DialectForge's dynamic dialect negotiation is designed to solve injection at the protocol level. New NIST guidelines emphasize red-teaming for multi-agent environments.

sections.label: COMPUTE & INFRASTRUCTURE
sections.text: NVIDIA Blackwell ramp faces continued delays. Google and Microsoft announce joint hyperscale builds in Texas while TSMC expands Arizona capacity for custom AI silicon.

sections.label: STRATEGIC QUESTION
sections.text: Will the first company to deploy 10M H100-equivalent compute achieve decisive AGI lead by 2028?
